summary: Burst of 5xx errors from FD exhaustion caused by half-closed socket storm (client lib 2.3.0)
description:
Issue summary:
During an evening traffic surge on 2026-03-10 we observed a tight ~18-minute window where a subset of tenant traffic (Finora Health) triggered a sharp increase in 5xx responses at the API gateway. Upstreams (serving runtime) were reporting process-level errors and eventually OOM/FD-exhaustion-like failures.

Impact:
- Finora Health experienced ~9% request failure rate for generation/chat endpoints during the window.
- Elevated customer error alerts and automated failover to fallback model variants triggered additional capacity pressure.
- Production latency spiked for affected routes.

Environment:
- Production (us-east-1) - dedicated tenant fleet for Finora Health on dedicated-capacity cluster.
- API Gateway version: apigw-1.9.3, Ingress proxy: envoy-2.4.1, Serving runtime: runtime-3.2.0
- Client SDK observed: finora-es-client v2.3.0 (newer behavior observed after rollout to some clients).

Steps to reproduce (approximate):
1) Simulate concurrent short-lived streaming sessions with frequent client-side half-close (RST) events and keepalive-negotiation churn.
2) Run a high fan-out of short generation requests (~600 req/s concentrated to the tenant shard) with the same client library behavior.
3) Observe connection table growth and rising FD usage on ingress/worker processes, then errors when FD limit reached.

Observed behavior:
- API Gateway returned 502/503/504 for requests routed to the impacted shard.
- Ingress and runtime logs show many connections in CLOSE_WAIT and a spike in open file descriptors.
- Kernel logs showed "EMFILE" type messages and runtime processes logged "failed to accept: too many open files" followed by worker restarts.
- Post-incident profiling indicated ~85% of FDs were sockets in TIME_WAIT/CLOSE_WAIT and not being reclaimed quickly due to client half-close behavior and short keepalive TTLs.

Relevant logs / excerpts:
- apigw: "error accepting conn: accept: too many open files" (multiple workers across nodes)
- ingress-proxy: "socket close-wait count=4123; max-fd=8192"
- runtime: "watchdog: process restart after uncaught OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files"
- kernel: "pid 4112: open files: 8765 (max 8192)"

Workaround applied during incident:
- Emergency increase of system FD limit on affected nodes (temporary) and rolling restart of ingress proxies to clear stale CLOSE_WAIT sockets.
- Activated tenant-level egress rate limiter to spread the Finora Health burst across longer window.
- Deployed a short-term apigw config change to lower concurrent connection per-worker acceptance rate to reduce FD growth.

Expected next steps / follow-up (see resolution):
- Root cause analysis and permanent mitigations completed (connection handling hardening + client coordination).
- Customer notified and incident postmortem published.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: generic 'thundering herd' causing runtime OOMs. However kernel-level EMFILE hints shifted focus to FD exhaustion. We observed correlation with Finora SDK version 2.3.0 rollout (client-side change in keepalive/close behavior).

Key findings:
- The client library started issuing aggressive TCP RST after streaming blocks in v2.3.0 for connection pooling efficiency. This produced many half-closed sockets on our side which lingered in CLOSE_WAIT.
- Ingress proxy (Envoy) configured with default delayed-close times and a relatively low worker FD budget led to resource starvation when hundreds of clients exhibited the new behavior simultaneously.
- The serving runtime did not enforce strict per-process FD reservation; combined with large model cache pages and logs this led to accept() failing and restarts.

Evidence collected:
- Packet captures show RSTs from client side immediately after upload shards.
- Node-level lsof and ss snapshots during the window showed >60% sockets in CLOSE_WAIT.
- Metrics show sudden jump in socket_open_count, fd_usage_percent, and worker_restart_count synchronized with increased 5xx.

Mitigation trials during incident:
- Increased process ulimit, restarted ingress to reclaim sockets: immediate drop in 5xx but not sustainable as long-term fix.
- Back-pressure via tenant rate limiter: reduced immediate FD pressure.
- Short-lived change to Envoy delayed_close to aggressively close sockets resulted in fewer lingering CLOSE_WAIT entries.

Post-incident reproduction notes:
- We reproduced locally using a synthetic client that closes streams with RST and observed identical FD accumulation in an Envoy+runtime composition.
resolution:
Permanent mitigations implemented and validated on 2026-03-12:
1) Ingress (Envoy) config patch to tune delayed_close, aggressive_linger_timeout, and per-worker fd soft-reservations deployed to prod us-east-1.
2) Serving runtime hardening: added FD guard that refuses new accepts when fd_usage exceeds 70% and responds with 429s (back-pressure) instead of allowing accept()/crash.
3) Operator playbook: new runbook steps for detecting CLOSE_WAIT storms and graduated mitigation (rate-limit -> system ulimit bump -> safe-restart).
4) Coordinated with Finora Health: flagged client SDK v2.3.0 and requested a staged rollback / follow-on patch to change RST behavior; client agreed and released v2.3.1 with recommended keepalive behavior.
5) Added alerting rule on fd_usage_percent > 65% and new dashboard panels for CLOSE_WAIT counts per node.

Customer communication:
- Finora Health SRE and account team were notified within the incident window; a post-incident summary and recommended client changes were shared. Customer acceptance of fixes confirmed on 2026-03-13.

Status: Resolved. All mitigations validated and monitoring in place.

follow_up_actions: Track adoption of client SDK v2.3.1 by Finora Health and other large tenants (30-day window)
Roll out Envoy config adjustments to eu-west and ap-south after validation (scheduled)
Add automated simulation test for half-close socket storms to CI for ingress/runtime combos
Document recommended client SDK socket/keepalive settings in DevX guides
notes_for_billing_and_cx: Customer experienced 18-minute interruption with ~9% error rate on affected endpoints. Support provided credit proposal pending Finance review (ticket FIN-0421). Account team to follow up on goodwill credit and technical verification in 7 days.
